description:
Ember Atlas is an independent research and technology project focused on transforming NASA Earth observation data into actionable environmental intelligence.

Our mission is to harmonize MODIS and VIIRS active fire observations, enabling more consistent historical analysis, improved visualization of wildfire patterns, and identification of unusual burning activity.
summary:
Ember Atlas produces one burning-activity calendar from 2000 to today that does not jump when satellites change. We harmonize 26 years of NASA FIRMS detections (MODIS C6.1 on Terra/Aqua, VIIRS 375 m C2 on Suomi-NPP/NOAA-20/NOAA-21) across nine regions using a Poisson panel with three separated effects: year-month activity, platform sensitivity, and a per-platform slope in local solar time.

The drift slope is identified because Terra and Aqua slide in opposite directions after 2022 while NOAA-20/21 hold their overpass time — that fixed platform anchors the year-month effect. Terra loses ~45% of its detections by 2026 purely from orbit drift, not fire change. The reference is Aqua afternoon, so the pre-2012 MODIS-only decade joins the VIIRS era on the same MODIS-equivalent scale.

The app shows the monthly calendar, anomaly against each month's own history, the overpass drift, the 2012 sensor step, and a MODIS-denial validation (−0.6% median error on Pantanal). It answers the operational question fire managers ask: "is this month normal for this region?" MODIS ends Jan 2027; this keeps 26 years of fire history alive.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Ember Atlas is a static, dependency-free web app that lets early-warning responders, land managers, and scientists visualize 26 years of harmonized fire activity for any of nine pre-built regions (Pantanal, Chilecito, Southern Amazon, Cerrado, Gran Chaco, Northern California, South-east Australia, Iberian Peninsula, Central Siberia). Users read a month-by-year calendar, switch to anomaly view (each month vs its own median/p10-p90 history), and export CSV. No login, no backend.

HOW IT WORKS

Raw FIRMS detections (MOD14, MYD14, VNP14IMGTDL, VJ114IMGTDL) are aggregated per calendar month, per satellite, day and night apart, with local solar time preserved. We fit a Poisson panel: log(E[n]) = α_satellite + γ_year-month + β_satellite × ΔLST, where ΔLST is the deviation from each satellite's 2012-2021 baseline. Terra's slope is ~8× Aqua's because Terra passes during the steep morning rise while Aqua passes near the afternoon plateau. Near-real-time rows are flagged "nrt" and used only for the most recent months; science-quality rows drive the fit.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

- Removes the ×9 instrument step at 2012 (raw jumps, harmonized does not)

- Recovers ~45% of Terra detections lost to orbital drift by 2026

- Enables the operational question: "is this month normal for this region?"

- Preserves 26 years of fire history across the MODIS-to-VIIRS transition (MODIS ends Jan 2027, Aqua ~Sep 2027)

- Supports CONAE-style early-warning workflows (inspired by the Chilecito Jul 2026 fire shown in the challenge brief)

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

Python 3.12, DuckDB (spatial + httpfs extensions), NumPy, pandas. The web app is vanilla JS with inline SVG — no framework, no build step, no CDN, opens from file://. Data sourced from the Portolan GeoParquet mirror of NASA FIRMS (cloud-native archive of the same LANCE products). Deployed on Vercel and GitHub Pages.

CREATIVITY

The per-platform slope in local solar time is original. Published harmonizations either use fixed ratios (which absorb drift as sensitivity) or complex footprint models. Our approach separates three effects cleanly and uses NOAA-20/21 as an overpass-time anchor to identify the drift.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

- MODIS-denial validation: train to 2018, rebuild 2019+ from VIIRS alone, compare with observed Aqua

- Color-blind-safe palettes (Okabe-Ito, viridis, diverging)

- Honest disclosure of limitations: no cloud-cover correction, sparse regions (Chilecito), Black Summer 2019-20 outside calibration distribution

- Static deployment so judges can open without login
